candidates.draft_title: Fix weekly digest showing aggregate stats for non-member teams when user has dual membership
candidates.snippet:
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: The weekly digest email. You know the one — the Monday "here's your team's activity this week" summary that goes to members. Several of my dual-team people are getting numbers that aren't theirs.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: So. I have a scientist, Aleksander, who's on Discovery and on Basel Launch. His Monday digest showed him the aggregate stats — session counts, average goals-completed, engagement rate — for a team he is not on. Not Discovery, not Basel Launch. A third team entirely. The "Formulation" team, which he has nothing to do with.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: Correct. And here's what makes it worse than just "wrong number." Those are aggregate stats for a team he's not a member of. So he's now seeing, in his inbox, how the Formulation team is doing. Their engagement rate. How many sessions they collectively booked. That's not his to see.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: Right. In a biotech, team-level performance data is sensitive. If the Formulation team is having a rough quarter, that's between them and their lead. It should absolutely not be surfacing in some random scientist's weekly email because he happens to be double-teamed.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: Good question. For Aleksander it's been Formulation two Mondays running. But I've got another dual-team person, Fenna, and hers showed a different wrong team than her actual two. So it's not like everyone's seeing Formulation — it's that dual-team people are getting some other team's numbers, and it's the wrong team per person.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: That's the pattern, yes. Single-team people seem fine — I asked around, and everyone whose digest I could check who's on exactly one team got their own correct numbers. It's specifically the dual-membership folks whose digest goes sideways.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: It surfaced when Aleksander emailed me two Mondays ago and said "why am I getting the Formulation team's stats." I hadn't been looking. Once he flagged it I checked the other dual-team people and found Fenna's. So — call it early June is when I have hard evidence, but it could've been happening since the reorg and nobody said anything.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: That's the part that got MY attention. I don't love that a person can see another team's aggregate performance because of how membership overlaps. If my legal team hears "members can see other teams' data," that becomes a whole thing.
[EXTERNAL] Priyanka: Aleksander definitely kept his, he's the type. I'll get you both IDs, the dates, and whatever screenshots exist by end of day.
